messages:
Priya Nair: Heads-up — onboarding Axial-13B conversion from Llama -> Gemma/Qwen. After int4 quant+proj reorder we see a consistent rotary phase 'blip' at head groups 4-6. Low-level diffs look like a phase offset, not random noise.
Jin Park: Can you paste a minimal failing example and the conversion command? @Priya
Priya Nair: repro prompt and command below. small output diff shows token-level drift after ~32 tokens.
```
# conversion
python convert.py --src llama-axial-13b.ckpt --dst gemma/axial13b.onnx --swap-proj-order --quant int4
```
```
Input: "In 2024 the results show"
Llama fp16 (gold): "...growth of 3.2% over last quarter."
Quantized Gemma int4: "...growth of 3.2% over last quarte­r." (soft hyphen inserted, rotary phase mismatch around token index 34)
```
Sam Torres: soft hyphen + odd punctuation often points at tokenizer/vocab normalization differences or a byte-level rewrite during conversion. Did you run NFKC on vocab?
Priya Nair: Not explicitly. We used the upstream converter that maps ids by surface string match. I suspect a tokenizer normalization mismatch plus a small headwise rotary scale change after reproj.
Ari Gomez: Two quick checks: 1) run the conversion with `--preserve-vocab` (no remap) and feed the same tokenizer artifact; 2) run fp16->int8 as a sanity (if int8 matches fp16 mostly then int4 quant is amplifying some headwise scale mismatch).
Priya Nair: Done quick tests: preserve-vocab + int8 -> much smaller drift, int4 still shows phase step. So quantization amplitude seems to amplify the mismatch.
Kai Liu: I bisected to a recent change in the proj reorder patch — commit 9c4f2d added a head-group permutation to optimize GEMM layout. That changes how rotary angles map per-head when we do per-head quant scale. If int4 uses different per-tensor scales, the head permutation + per-head scale mismatch equals a phase blip.
Jin Park: Good catch. So options: (A) use a consistent headwise scale mapping after permute (remap scales), (B) apply a small corrective rotary head-scale factor before quantizing, or (C) quantize with symmetric per-tensor scale for rotary-related kernels.
Priya Nair: I tried remapping scales by undoing the permute for rotary angles before quant and reapplying after load — immediate improvement: token delta reduced by ~70% on the smoke prompt.
ci-bot: test/rotary-compat-smoke passed: 18/20 prompts within tolerance (baseline fp16).
Sam Torres: Are there any vocab aliasing cases? The soft hyphen in the earlier diff suggests the tokenizer produced a different codepoint sequence post-conversion. Could be unicode normalization + byteorder in tokenizer export.
Ari Gomez: Also check KV cache indexing offsets — if token ids shift by +1/−1 for certain sentinel tokens, the KVCACHE could be pulling wrong cached keys, which interacts badly with rotary phase at long context.
Priya Nair: Added a tight test: run long-context generation with identical token ids streamed from the same tokenizer instance (no re-tokenize). That eliminated soft-hyphen drift but not the phase blip entirely — so two orthogonal issues: vocab normalization and head-scale/permute.
Kai Liu: For a robust patch I propose: 1) canonicalize tokenizer export to NFKC and include a checksum in model metadata, 2) add an option `--remap-rotary-scales` in converter that remaps per-head scales to post-permute ordering, 3) add an int4 quant mode that ties rotary kernels to per-tensor symmetric scale fallback.
Jin Park: Agreed. Also add a small regression test: generate with a set of prompts that stress long-context and include punctuation that tends to produce combined codepoints. Put into CI under eng-ml/rotary-compat.
Priya Nair: I'll open PR with the remap and a failing->fixed unit test. Quick notes for PR: attach numeric bisect results, perf impact (remap adds ~0.2ms per-token for converter only), and the smoke vector of 20 prompts.
Sam Torres: One more experiment: try a headwise multiplicative correction pre-quant of `angle *= head_scale_correction[head]` where head_scale_correction is computed from a tiny calibration set. If that removes residual phase offset we can avoid heavier converter changes while we land the remap.
Priya Nair: Running calibration now. Early run: correction reduces RMS logit diff by ~15% beyond remap. Will include numbers in PR.
Ari Gomez: Nice. After PR we should run full eval (LLM-eval harness) across openset benchmarks and hallucination checks — ensure no regression in summarization quality.
Priya Nair: Yep. Plan: PR with remap + unit tests + optional headwise correction flag. Owner: @Priya for implementation, @Jin for tests, @Kai for perf review, @Sam for tokenizer checksum. Target: ship to staging quant builds by EOW. :rocket:
